sources.snippet: Sep 12, 2026 · What is the EU AI Act? The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is the world's first comprehensive horizontal legal framework for artificial intelligence. It entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies progressively across four risk tiers. The Act uses a risk-based approach: the higher the potential harm, the stricter the obligations.

sources.snippet: THE EU AI ACT OVERVIEW OF KEY RULES AND REQUIREMENTS On 12 July 2024, the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) was finally published in the EU’s Official Journal1, marking the conclusion of a long elaboration and adoption process.

answer:
The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies progressively across four risk tiers [2]. It is fully enforceable since 2 August 2026, when the AI Office and national regulators began supervising it and new transparency rules for chatbots, deepfakes and AI-generated content took effect [4].

Prohibitions, definitions and AI literacy obligations became applicable on 2 February 2025 [1]. Governance rules and obligations for general-purpose AI models became applicable on 2 August 2025 [1]. GPAI providers must keep up-to-date technical documentation, inform downstream providers, respect EU copyright law, and publish a summary of training content [3]. Transparency requirements under Article 50 and innovation support measures apply from 2 August 2026, when enforcement started [1]. Obligations for high-risk systems in Annex III apply from 2 December 2027, and obligations for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from 2 August 2028 [1].

The full roll-out is complete by 2 August 2028 [1]. The 2026 omnibus amendments deferred high-risk obligations [2]. A ninth prohibition covering AI-generated non-consensual sexually explicit content or child sexual abuse material takes effect in December 2026, along with machine-readable marking on generative AI systems already on the market [4].
